description: A market-rate apartment building sized for a harsh-winter market, where indoor amenities carry more weight than outdoor ones and parking is still required for financing.

departments.name: Residential Units
departments.description: Private, restful, the majority of rentable area

departments.name: Community & Amenity
departments.description: High-energy, social — a major driver of occupancy and retention in a cold climate

spaces.name: Main Lobby & Lounge
spaces.notes: Secure vestibule, ride-share waiting area, fireplace lounge

spaces.name: Co-working Studio
spaces.notes: Open work tables, private zoom pods, coffee bar

spaces.name: Fitness & Wellness
spaces.notes: Cardio, free weights, flex studio for yoga/stretching

spaces.name: Rooftop Club Room
spaces.notes: Indoor entertaining space with skyline views, adjacent to outdoor deck

spaces.name: Package Room
spaces.notes: High-capacity automated lockers and oversized package shelving

spaces.name: Pet Spa
spaces.notes: Two washing stations and a grooming table

spaces.name: Leasing & Admin
spaces.notes: Two leasing desks, private property manager office, staff break area

spaces.name: MEP Rooms
spaces.notes: Main electrical switchgear, water service, boiler room, elevator machine rooms

spaces.name: Trash & Recycling
spaces.notes: Ground-floor compactor room aligned with trash chutes from upper floors

spaces.name: Maintenance Shop
spaces.notes: Tool storage, paint supply, workbench for the building engineer

departments.name: Transit & Parking
departments.description: Required for financing even where policy pushes toward walking, cycling, and transit

spaces.name: Vehicle Parking
spaces.notes: 0.6 spaces per unit; includes drive aisles and ramps at ~350 SF per stall

spaces.name: Secure Bike Room
spaces.notes: Wall-mounted and floor racks, plus a D.I.Y. bike repair stand and pump
